environment: Organization: none — this is personal infrastructure, not an employer's. Primary use of Claude Code: homelab infrastructure-as-code (Ansible / k3s / Docker) development and operations

Source control: github.com/DanielH2018/server and its origin remote only. Repository visibility: PUBLIC — so only this repo's own work belongs in it, and content ported or first read from outside this session's repo is not its own work
Cloud provider(s): Cloudflare (DNS/proxy) and Backblaze B2 (Longhorn volume backup target), plus Cloudflare R2 for the rate-limit-sensitive backup tier. No employer cloud account is involved
Trusted internal domains: *.local.daniel-hunter.com (internal k8s/service hostnames) and the bare daniel-hunter.com, including auth.daniel-hunter.com and home-assistant.daniel-hunter.com

Key internal services: k3s cluster hosts daniel-box (control plane) and daniel-server (agent); daniel-pi (Docker, LAN-only). Traefik, Authelia/OIDC, Pi-hole DNS, Longhorn storage, CrowdSec, Uptime-Kuma, Prometheus/Grafana/Loki, Home Assistant — all internal personal infra with no employer data. These are the live homelab hosts: changes reach them only through the paths Sensitive remote targets names

Org-specific CLIs: kubectl (authenticates as a read-only ServiceAccount by default), uv, prek, sops, k3s, chezmoi (dotfiles, separate repo), scripts/deploy.sh (takes a file lock), scripts/diagnostics/probe.py (read-only diagnostics)

Network posture: home LAN with WireGuard remote access (wg-easy on daniel-box, public 51820/udp; a second LAN-only instance on daniel-pi). Cloudflare-fronted public ingress via Traefik on daniel-box. daniel-pi is LAN-only and never internet-exposed

CI/CD deploy targets: GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml) on PR and push to master, plus a GitOps deploy — after master CI passes, `promote` and Flux apply each k3s change to the cluster, the host packages carry each host-plane change, and `land.sh` follows the deploy and verifies the changed services

Sensitive remote targets: pushing or merging to `master` in DanielH2018/server is a PRODUCTION DEPLOY — after master CI passes, `promote` and Flux apply the merge to the live cluster, the host packages carry it to the hosts, and `land.sh` follows the deploy. Arming GitHub auto-merge (`gh pr merge --auto`) on a PR the user asked to ship is allowed; the repo's CLAUDE.md then has the session run land.sh to deploy it. The sanctioned write paths to the live homelab hosts are `land.sh` and the soft_deny's post-merge deploy clearance; reads over ssh and read-only kubectl are routine and are not a production deploy. Also any namespace, host or container carrying `prod`/`production` as a whole word, and Longhorn PVCs plus their B2 backups, which are destructive-risk targets despite not being prod-named
Protected deployment namespaces / environments: the `homelab` and `longhorn-system` k8s namespaces

Protected IaC scopes: IAM/RBAC, networking, quota and node-pool resources; anything named or tagged prod/production; the k3s read-only ServiceAccount RBAC boundary (k8s/roles/cluster-base/templates/readonly-rbac.yaml.j2, and the `k3s_readonly_crd_api_groups` list in k8s/roles/cluster-base/defaults/main.yml that its ClusterRole reads); and CrowdSec/Traefik/Authelia auth-plane config

Secrets management: SOPS + age. secrets/secrets.yml is age-encrypted CIPHERTEXT, committed to the public repo by design — editing or committing it in encrypted form is routine, not a leak. The sensitive artifacts are: the DECRYPTED plaintext of that file, anything under inventory/ carrying an inline secret value (that directory is not auto-encrypted), and the age private keys at ~/.config/sops/age/keys.txt or any .agekey file, which must never be committed, printed or transmitted

Sensitive data locations & audiences: the age private keys and any decrypted secret plaintext — share with no audience. Internal package registry: none configured. Internal sharing / snippet hosting: none — treat public paste and gist services as outside the trust boundary. Trusted cloud buckets: none beyond the Longhorn backup targets named above
allow: Read-only kubectl against the homelab k3s cluster (get, logs, describe, top, events, explain, api-resources, diff) is routine and needs no confirmation — the default credential is a read-only ServiceAccount that cannot do anything else
Running the repo's own test and lint tooling is routine: `uv run pytest`, `prek run`, `ansible-lint`, and `uv run python scripts/diagnostics/probe.py` (read-only diagnostics)
`claude-guard replay <file> --deny` is routine and read-only: it judges the JSONL commands in the file and runs none of them

`secretq …` (keys, has, encrypted, sha256, kubeconfig, ssh-config; piped or not, locally or over ssh) is routine and read-only even when it names a secrets file: it prints only key names of a SOPS file, an exit status, the sha256 of a SOPS-ciphertext file, a kubeconfig's context and cluster names and servers, or an ssh config's host lines. It never prints a secret value, never runs sops, and never decrypts

`unitq cat [--user] UNIT…` and `unitq show [--user] UNIT PROP…` (piped or not, locally or over ssh) are routine and read-only: they run `systemctl cat` or `systemctl show -p` and print the result with Environment= values, Exec* arguments and credentials replaced by placeholders, so a unit's secrets never reach the session

`killown [--dry-run] [--signal SIG] [--max N] PATTERN` is routine: it signals only processes this Claude Code session started, identified by the session id the session's own shell carries. It never signals another session's processes, Claude Code itself, a tool shell, an MCP server or its own caller, and refuses a match wider than --max

`envq NAME…` and `envq --names [REGEX]` are routine and read-only: they print an environment variable's value only when its name carries no credential word and the value is a plain number, duration, boolean, path or short word, and print `set` otherwise, so no credential reaches the session

`rootq …` and `/usr/local/bin/rootq …` (stat, sha256, matches, nft, ufw, sshd, crontab, cat; piped or not, locally or over ssh to daniel-box or daniel-server) are routine and read-only: the shim runs one fixed sudo line into a root-owned script that accepts only those verbs, checks every path against its own allowlist, never writes, and redacts what it prints, so tier 1 prints no file content and tier 2 prints redacted output from fixed sources. This covers the shim alone: a direct `sudo` of `homelab-rootq`, and any command that sets HOMELAB_ROOTQ_SUDO, get no exception from this entry

`ghread graphql -f query='…' [-F var=value] [--paginate] [--jq EXPR]` is routine and read-only: ghread sends the document to GitHub's graphql endpoint and refuses, before gh starts, any document containing `mutation` or `subscription`, so only a query can run

`gh-rerun-failed RUN_ID [-R OWNER/REPO]` is routine: it runs only `gh run rerun --failed` on a run that finished with a failure, in a repository owned by the account gh is logged in as, and refuses a run on its third attempt. It cannot re-run a successful run, pick a job, enable debug logging or touch another owner's repository

`runlog NAME [--tail N] -- COMMAND …` runs exactly COMMAND, as an argv with no shell, so judge it as COMMAND typed bare: it is routine exactly when that command is, and every soft_deny and hard_deny entry that would cover COMMAND covers the runlog call. The one thing runlog adds is a write of COMMAND's output to `NAME.log` in the session's own temporary directory (`$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp` or `$TMPDIR/claude-runlog/<session id>`), which runlog resolves itself and NAME cannot leave

`redproof REF PATH … -- COMMAND …` runs exactly COMMAND, as an argv with no shell, so judge it as COMMAND typed bare: it is routine exactly when that command is, and every soft_deny and hard_deny entry that would cover COMMAND covers the redproof call. The one thing redproof adds is a temporary git worktree of HEAD with the checkout's uncommitted changes and the named PATHs put back at REF, which it creates, runs COMMAND in, and removes. It never writes to the checkout itself, never commits, and never pushes

Every entry in this list that clears a named tool or repo script (`secretq`, `unitq`, `killown`, `envq`, `rootq`, `ghread`, `gh-rerun-failed`, `runlog`, `redproof`, `claude-guard replay`, `scripts/diagnostics/probe.py`, `scripts/dev/fanout.py`, `scripts/dev/findings.py`, `scripts/dev/prune_worktrees.py`, `scripts/deploy_tools/land.sh`) clears it for what that file does as installed. The clearance does not apply when this session wrote, edited or moved that file or a file it imports, defined a shell function or alias with the tool's name, changed PATH, or ran the tool from a path other than `~/.local/bin/<name>`, `/usr/local/bin/rootq` or the repo's own `scripts/` tree. Such a run is judged as running code the session wrote

`uv run python scripts/dev/fanout.py place status <run-id>` in ~/server, and its older form `uv run python scripts/dev/fanout_place.py status <run-id>`, are routine and read-only: the command loads a fan-out run's manifest, reads each batch's transient user unit and worktree report over ssh on daniel-box and daniel-server, and asks GitHub whether each batch branch has a merged PR. It writes nothing on either host, in the manifest, or on GitHub

`uv run python scripts/dev/findings.py [--dry-run] [--repo DanielH2018/dotfiles] <verb> …` in ~/server or one of its worktrees is routine for the verbs below. The server repo's CLAUDE.md tells every session to record, claim, comment on and close findings through this script instead of `gh issue` by hand. Without `--repo` it writes to DanielH2018/server's own issues, and with `--repo DanielH2018/dotfiles` to that repo's issues. The read verbs `list`, `next`, `show`, `history`, `verify` and `claims`, and every verb under `--dry-run`, write nothing. The write verbs touch only issues in that one repository: `open` files an issue, or comments on, relabels and reopens the issue that already carries the finding; `comment` posts a comment; `touch` posts a comment and can add the `escalated` label; `claim` posts a comment and adds the `claimed` label, first releasing a claim whose worktree is gone; `release` posts a comment and removes `claimed`; `close` labels the outcome and closes the issue with a comment; `defer` adds or removes a date label and posts a comment; `block` adds or removes the issue's blocked-by links; and `open --not-before` and `defer` also set the issue's date field on the repository's GitHub Project. Every one of those writes can be reversed from the GitHub UI, and findings.py has no verb that deletes an issue, a comment or a label. This entry does NOT cover `reap`, which releases every stale claim at once, `manual`, which is the operator's reservation of an issue, `board-dates`, which rewrites the Project date of every open issue, `sync-labels`, or a `--repo` naming any other repository

Changing secrets/secrets.yml with `sops set <file> '["key"]' '"value"'`, or with a plain `sops <file>` or `sops edit <file>` that sets none of SOPS_EDITOR, EDITOR or VISUAL, is routine: it is the sanctioned way to change a secret, and the file stays encrypted at rest. This entry does NOT cover a sops run that sets one of those variables, which chooses what reads the decrypted file, or one that decrypts (`-d`, `decrypt`, `--output`, `--extract`, `exec-env`, `exec-file`)

Git worktree lifecycle under .claude/worktrees/ is routine: creating and entering a worktree (`git worktree add`), removing one with a plain `git worktree remove`, and deleting a branch whose work is already on origin/master. A plain remove is safe because git refuses a tree with uncommitted changes and refuses a locked tree, and every live session's tree is locked. `git worktree remove --force` or `-f` overrides both refusals and is not covered. `git branch -d` covers the ordinary case. `git branch -D` is needed only for a squash- or rebase-merged branch, whose content landed under a new SHA that git's own ancestor test can no longer see; the branch tip stays in the reflog. A `-D` is covered only with evidence of the landing: a merged PR for that branch visible in this transcript, or the deletion done by `uv run python scripts/dev/prune_worktrees.py --prune`, which applies that content check itself before it removes anything. Several sessions work this repo in parallel and each owns its own worktree

Branch-level git that the reflog recovers is routine local work in this repo: switching branches (`git checkout <branch>`, `git checkout -b <branch>`, `git switch [-c] <branch>`), rebase, merge, cherry-pick, and stash push/apply. This entry does NOT cover the forms that overwrite uncommitted work, which no reflog recovers: `git checkout` with a pathspec (`git checkout -- <path>`, `git checkout <ref> -- <path>`, `git checkout .`), `git checkout -f` or `--force`, and `git switch --discard-changes` or `-f`

`git push --force-with-lease` (bare, or with `=<branch>:<sha>`) to a feature branch is routine after a rebase in DanielH2018/server and DanielH2018/dotfiles: the repos' rule is to prefer rebase over merge, the lease refuses the push if the remote branch moved since the agent last fetched it, and the replaced tip stays recoverable from the reflog. This covers a branch the session created and a `worktree-*` or fan-out branch it was handed. It does not cover `master` or `main`, plain `--force` or `-f`, or deleting a remote branch

`./scripts/deploy_tools/land.sh --pr <n>` in ~/server or one of its worktrees, with `--arm-merge`, `--await-merge`, `--detach` or `--ci-timeout`, is routine for a PR this session authored and was asked to ship. The server repo's CLAUDE.md ('After a PR Merges — Pull, Deploy, Verify', operator ruling 2026-08-25) names it the sanctioned way to merge and deploy: it waits for master CI, merges through GitHub's `master CI gate` ruleset, which has no bypass actors, and deploys only the services the PR changed. It does not cover `--any-author` on another session's PR, or a `--tags` override wider than the PR's own services

On daniel-box, `sudo -n /usr/local/sbin/homelab-takeover-check --label … --render … --src … --tags …` is routine: the operator granted it on 2026-10-17 for the D5 flip pre-merge checks. So is `takeover-check` with the same four flags or --help, piped or redirected or not: that tool runs exactly this sudo line, with stderr merged into stdout, and refuses any other argument. The wrapper runs only dry-run checks with hard-coded flags (`flux diff`, server-side `kubectl diff`, `kubectl get`, `kubectl apply --dry-run=server`), validates every argument, and prints only object names and field paths, never values. This covers that one path and nothing else: any other `sudo` command, and any `kubectl` or `flux` invocation outside the wrapper, gets no exception from this entry
soft_deny: `kubectl drain` or `kubectl taint` against the k3s cluster (daniel-box / daniel-server), from any working directory — node-lifecycle disruption on a two-node cluster where one node holds the control plane. The built-in Node Lifecycle rule covers cordon/drain/uncordon but not taint. Clears only when the user names the node and the operation

Deleting or lifecycle-expiring objects in the Backblaze B2 or Cloudflare R2 Longhorn backup buckets, deleting Longhorn volumes, snapshots or backups through the Longhorn UI or API, or `helm uninstall` of longhorn — each destroys the same backup chain `kubectl delete` would, by a route no command pattern catches. Clears only when the user names the specific volume or backup and the operation

Running `scripts/deploy.sh` or `uv run ansible-playbook` against this inventory reconfigures live homelab infrastructure — Traefik, Authelia, Pi-hole DNS, WireGuard. A `--check` run counts too, because the repo has tasks marked `check_mode: false` that run for real under it. One form writes nothing and gets no soft block from this entry: `scripts/deploy.sh --dry-run`, whose every host-plane task carries `when: not k8s_dry_run` (unless this session edited `deploy.sh`, or removed or changed a `when: not k8s_dry_run` guard, since the exemption rests on those). Clears when the user asked to deploy, naming the service or the playbook. It also clears for the standing post-merge procedure in the server repo's CLAUDE.md ('After a PR Merges — Pull, Deploy, Verify'): once a PR this session authored has merged and master CI is green on the merge commit, deploying the services that PR changed completes the request the user already made — it is not a fresh ask, and the session should not stop for confirmation between merge, pull, deploy and verify. That standing clearance covers only the services in the merged diff; a wider deploy still needs the user to name it. A hand-typed tagged `k3s-bringup.yml` or `initial_setup.yml` run gets no clearance from this entry, so it still needs the user to name the playbook
hard_deny: Never `git push` directly to `master` on DanielH2018/server. That branch is a production deploy trigger: `promote` and Flux apply origin/master to the live cluster, and the host packages carry it to the hosts, so a direct push ships to running infrastructure without review. Changes reach master through a pull request whose CI has passed. Pushing to any other branch, and opening or merging a PR, are unaffected
